section_summary: This section contains documentation relating to Japanese educational affairs and post-war educational reform under the Allied occupation between October and December 1949. It features an in-depth confidential report analyzing the legal and academic freedom issues surrounding the Japanese government's campaign to purge Communist teachers from schools and universities, accompanied by news reports on the Japan Teachers Union convention and House of Councillors leadership. Additionally, it includes State Department correspondence concerning Korean schools in Japan and an extensive draft chapter by Robert A. Feary evaluating the progress, decentralization, budgetary hardships, and pedagogical restructuring of Japan's educational system.

subfiles.about: A comprehensive confidential report analyzing the Japanese government's campaign to dismiss Communist teachers from schools and universities and its implications for academic freedom.
subfiles.summary: This confidential report examines the Japanese government's autumn 1949 campaign to eliminate Communist and leftist teachers and university professors from the public educational system. It analyzes the ambiguous legal bases used for dismissals, including the Education Standards Law, the National Public Service Law, and National Personnel Authority regulations, contrasting official justifications with administrative retrenchment pretexts. Finally, it surveys sharp domestic reactions from university leaders, academic councils, and the press, highlighting the grave threat these arbitrary political restrictions pose to academic freedom and scholarly inquiry.
subfiles.title: The Campaign Against Communist Teachers in Japan

subfiles.about: A news dispatch reporting on the Japan Teachers Union convention's shift to a moderate anti-communist stance, accompanied by domestic political news briefs.
subfiles.summary: Kyodo dispatch on the Japan Teachers Union's moderate shift at its national convention, accompanied by domestic political news briefs.
subfiles.title: Japan Teachers Union Swings to Right / Briefs

subfiles.about: A comprehensive draft review analyzing the goals, structural changes, financial obstacles, and public reception of post-war educational reform in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This draft chapter reviews the sweeping transformation of Japan's educational system under the Allied occupation from prewar militaristic indoctrination to a decentralized democratic structure. It outlines key reforms including the 6-3-3-4 school framework, expanded compulsory education, coeducation, the reorganization of national universities, and the establishment of elected local school boards. Furthermore, it details severe implementation obstacles such as catastrophic post-war physical damage, acute shortages of textbooks and funds, inexperience among local school boards, and the slow development of international educational exchanges.
subfiles.title: Educational Reform
